definition: Braina is a virtual assistant and speech-to-text dictation application for Microsoft Windows developed by Brainasoft.
details: Braina uses natural language interface, speech synthesis, and speech recognition technology to interact with its users and allows them to use natural language sentences to perform various tasks on a computer. The name Braina is a short form of "Brain Artificial". Braina is marketed as a Microsoft Copilot alternative. It provides a voice interface for several locally run and cloud large language models, including the latest LLMs from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Meta, Mistral, etc; while improving data privacy. Braina also allows responses from its in-house large language models like Braina Swift and Braina Pinnacle. It has an "Artificial Brain" feature that provides persistent memory support for supported LLMs.

explainer.lead: Braina is a Windows application for controlling a computer and dictating text by voice. It also provides a voice interface to local and cloud large language models, with optional persistent memory for supported models.

tiers.eli5: Braina is like a helpful listener for a Windows computer: you speak to it, and it can write down your words or carry out requests. It can also connect your voice to different AI models, a bit like using one microphone to talk to several helpers.
tiers.practitioner: On Windows, Braina can be used for speech-to-text dictation, natural-language computer tasks, and voice interaction with locally run or cloud LLMs. Model choices include systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Meta, and Mistral, alongside Braina Swift and Braina Pinnacle. The Artificial Brain feature adds persistent memory only for supported LLMs, and using a cloud model still involves that provider rather than keeping processing local.
tiers.paperLevel: Braina can be described as a Windows interaction layer f: (speech input, selected LLM, optional persistent memory) -> (computer action, dictated text, or spoken response). Its components include speech recognition, a natural-language interface, speech synthesis, and connections to local or cloud LLMs. Persistent memory through Artificial Brain is limited to supported models.

explainer.example: A user speaks a request to Braina on a Windows PC. Braina recognizes the speech, passes the language request to a selected supported LLM, and speaks the model's answer aloud; if Artificial Brain is enabled for that model, relevant information can persist for later interactions.

explainer.intuition: Braina places speech and language between the user and the computer, so a request can be spoken instead of typed or clicked. It can route language-model interactions to different local or cloud models while keeping the same interface.
howItWorks: The user speaks a request or text to dictate.
Speech recognition converts the audio into text.
The natural-language interface interprets the request for a computer task or an LLM interaction.
A selected local, cloud, or in-house LLM can generate a response, with Artificial Brain supplying persistent memory where supported.
Braina performs the requested task or uses speech synthesis to speak the response.
explainer.whyItMatters: It combines dictation, voice control, and access to multiple LLMs in one Windows application. Local-model support can improve data privacy, while persistent memory can make supported assistants more continuous across interactions.
misconceptions: Braina is not just one LLM; it is an application that interfaces with several models and also offers its own.
Artificial Brain does not provide persistent memory for every LLM, only supported ones.
Choosing a local model can improve privacy, but cloud-model requests are not local processing.
